ACCO_2024q1.summary_analysis: ACCO Brands reported fourth-quarter and full-year 2023 results that beat expectations, but shares fell 12% on the day as investors reacted to weak 2024 guidance, according to the Motley Fool. Revenue and adjusted EPS both topped analyst estimates and gross margin improved, but the company guided first-quarter EPS well below the Street's estimate and cited a challenging macro environment and weaker-than-anticipated return-to-office trends behind its sales declines.
ACCO_2024q1.explicit_reasons: The Motley Fool said ACCO's 2024 guidance -- sales down 2% to 5% and first-quarter EPS of $0.01-$0.04 versus the $0.08 Wall Street expected -- underwhelmed investors and sent shares down 12% on the day.
ACCO_2024q1.implicit_reasons: Fourth-quarter revenue of $488.6 million and adjusted EPS of $0.39 both beat analyst estimates, and full-year gross margin improved 420 basis points despite lower sales; the company is also pursuing a restructuring program to cut at least $60 million in annual costs. ACCO attributed its sales declines to a challenging macroeconomic environment, lower-than-anticipated return-to-office trends, and tight retailer inventory management.

Guidance.text: ACCO guided to 2024 sales down 2% to 5% and first-quarter EPS of $0.01-$0.04, versus Wall Street's $0.08 estimate for the quarter; the Motley Fool said this guidance "underwhelmed" investors, sending shares down 12% on the day.

Revenue.text: Fourth-quarter revenue of $488.6 million beat Wall Street's estimate of $476 million (a 2.57% surprise versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate), even though sales were down 2.2% year over year and down 5.9% for the full year.

Profits, costs and margin.text: Adjusted EPS of $0.39 beat the $0.33 analyst estimate (an 18.18% surprise), and the company said full-year gross margin improved 420 basis points despite the revenue declines; ACCO is also pursuing a multiyear restructuring program targeting at least $60 million in annual cost cuts.

Macro and micro development.text: ACCO said the sales declines reflected "the challenging macroeconomic environment," "lower than anticipated return to office trends," and tight inventory management by retailers.
